params.body: View-space depth fades the sheet as the camera approaches (0.25–1.25 units). Depth Fade softens intersections with opaque scene geometry. These masks multiply the stripes and edges before Opacity clamps the final alpha to 0…1. Inspect the scene-depth branch in the main preview; its thumbnails are off.
params.title: Camera and intersection fades

params.body: Two Voronoi fields keep the motes fixed in UV space. Each cell supplies a random phase to a sine wave, so particles fade in and out at different times. Dust fade speed controls the cycle in radians per second (1.5 is about four seconds); 0 freezes the brightness. The ray alpha keeps the motes inside the shafts.
params.title: Fading dust

params.body: Distance from the UV center fades both sides and both ends. Multiply the two axes so the rectangular sheet disappears softly. The bottom fade also works when there is no floor behind the ray.
params.title: Feather the sheet

params.body: Add dust to the light, tint in linear space, and send it to an unlit, two-sided transparent material. Intensity changes brightness; Opacity changes visibility. Values above 1 preserve HDR highlights for bloom when the host scene provides it.
params.title: Warm transparent light

params.body: UV derivatives measure one render pixel on the plane. Two perpendicular vectors and their determinant convert the offset from a fixed particle center into screen pixels, including the sheet’s shear. Particle size is the diameter in render pixels, with a one-pixel soft edge. Centers and density stay attached to the plane; only size compensates for zoom and scale.
params.title: Particle size in pixels

params.body: After Cyanilux: cyanilux.com/tutorials/god-rays-shader-breakdown/. Use a plane. Flatten its Y to the foot of the sheet, then UV.y stretches its top toward the light in object space. Rotate the mesh to place it; this graph does not billboard or sample shadows.
params.title: Stretch toward the light

params.body: Sample noise across U only: keeping Y at zero stretches it into long stripes. Time moves through Z to slowly change their brightness. Density sets the number of shafts; Smoothstep and Power separate bright beams from the gaps.
params.title: Slowly shifting stripes
